ai.description: This frog reaches 30–35 mm. It is brown or yellowish-green with dark, irregular dorsal markings and a distinct white spot on the snout. It lacks vomerine teeth and has granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes ponmudi* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct white spots on its dark-colored belly and throat, which are absent in most similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: The Large Ponmudi Bush Frog inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large Ponmudi Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense foliage during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes ponmudi* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes ponmudi is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found at high elevations between 900 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Large Ponmudi Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tseep" call, typically heard as a series of rapid, repetitive notes from within dense, high-altitude shrubbery.
